## Orientation

Worktree only for code: /home/andrewyin/se-workflow--backlog-capture
Primary checkout (do not write .artifacts): /home/andrewyin/se-workflow
Edit only contract/project-design.json in the worktree; copy to worktree .artifacts/project-design.json and resolve there for local check if needed — parent owns primary store.
No concurrent wave-1 peers. Do not edit skills, dashboard, or tests except if contract self-consistency requires a tiny fix (prefer contract-only).
Use `command adaptive-artifacts` or the real binary if testing CLI; a shell wrapper may redirect --store to ~/.artifacts.

### Requirements
R1: The bundled contract defines `project:backlog-item` so deferred work can be created and listed in the store.
R3: A backlog item requires `payload.effort` naming a live or reopenable goal subject; `source` (and an external link in the body when useful) is optional.
R4: Status covers open work and the terminal outcomes promoted and dismissed, using current-status supersede.

### Design Invariants
- Feedback never stores deferred backlog.
- Structured promote never skips discuss for a new phase.
- Every backlog-item has an effort subject that names a goal area.
- Only `status=open` active items appear in handoff and the Backlog panel.
- Needs you never lists backlog items.

### Design Assumptions
- `current-status` supersede works like assessment and goals.
- Needs you prompt-copy and CLI dismiss patterns extend cleanly to backlog actions.
- No adaptive-artifacts runtime change is required.

### Decisions
- backlog-vs-feedback: New project:backlog-item; keep project:feedback unchanged
- backlog-effort-scope: payload.effort required on every backlog-item
- backlog-item-pattern: project:backlog-item uses current-status with supersede for status
